newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MINORCO, CVRD TO DEVELOP SALOBO.
newsitem.headline: MINORCO, CVRD TO DEVELOP SALOBO.

text.p: Minorco SA, the offshore arm of Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, said on Wednesday it had formed a new joint venture company with Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) to develop the Salobo copper and gold project in Brazil.

Minorco said its wholly-owned subsidiary Mineracao Morro Velho SA (MMV) had reached definitive agreement with CVRD and Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Economico e Social (BNDES) to transfer Salobo mineral rights to a newly-formed company, Salobo Metais SA (SMS).
Initial ownserhsip of SMS is shared between MMV and CVRD, but BNDES has the right to take up to a third, subject to its willingness to fund its share of pre-production capital.

SMS will now proceed with pre-implementation of the project which, if successful, will allow construction to go ahead, subject to certain conditions, including the negotiation of satisfactory third party finance.

Following completion of a feasibility study an investment of $1.5 billion -- or $2 billion including working capital, interest and escalated costs -- is estimated to bring the project into production over four years.

Annual production from the resource, in the Carajas region of Para state, is expected to be 200,000 tonnes of refined copper, 250,000 ounces of gold, together with silver and sulphuric acid. The mine is estimated to have an initial life of 33 years.
